evidence.claims: Every number checked against results.txt: table rows lag 0/5/10 backed; '5 of 16 cells' backed (but one is a printed -0.000 tie); 'every difference within 0.010 C' backed (max +0.010); 'bands only 0.1 to 0.2 C wide' backed; 'full 0.15-0.80 range' backed; '1.4 C adds 0.05-0.07 between, 0.02-0.04 outside, ours, lag 0 and 10' backed (0.074/0.046, 0.044/0.023); '3.0 C adds up to 0.14' backed (0.137); 'about 40 s' backed (26.5 s). The 'Why' paragraph is labelled a hypothesis. Limitations, AI-assistance note and 'model, not measured' are present and honest. Minor: 'the same first-order lag' is a forward-Euler update with a 1-min step (inherited), which responds faster than a continuous first-order lag with that time constant (0.730 vs 0.712 after 10 min at lag 5).
evidence.fitness: The negative result is sound and robust: a finer grid (lows every 0.05 C, widths 0.02-0.5 C, on/off widths 0-0.4 C; scripts/indep.py fine) gives the same answer, both families collapse onto the 33.7 C setpoint and differ by at most 0.008 C. But it is the textbook expectation: with no actuation cost and a pure regulation-error score, near-bang-bang is optimal, and a wider P-only band adds steady-state offset (Astrom and Murray, Feedback Systems, ch. 10-11; Astrom and Hagglund, PID controllers). No control literature is cited and no novelty holds beyond the repository. The open question the README leaves (switch cost) is answerable in seconds with the upstream penalty sweep: with garment-twonodelag's 0.01 C/switch penalty, proportional wins all four ours cells at lag 0 and 10 (-0.011 to -0.033 C; scripts/penalty.py), and the narrow on/off gate crosses the midpoint 14 and 24 times in the 20 C held-out scenarios vs 1 for proportional (scripts/indep.py chatter). One 49-line module, the 45th garment-* slug, rather than a step inside a programme (research/CLAUDE.md); far below the publishable bar.
evidence.domain: Against control practice: the comparison is fair in tuning budget and protocol (same train/held-out split, exhaustive grids), but a reviewer would ask for PI (named as untested), an actuation/switching cost (named as absent), a defined switch count for a continuous actuator (midpoint crossings is not one), and a continuous-time or exact-discretised lag rather than forward Euler. The score is |tsk-33.7|, explicitly a proxy, not PMV/ISO 7730 or a two-node thermal sensation model. Usable as a caveated what-if inside the chain; not a method a control engineer would sign off on as an answer to 'does proportional beat on/off'.

defects.what: The README leaves 'with a per-switch cost proportional control might help' as the open question, but the upstream garment-twonodelag penalty sweep answers it in seconds: at 0.01 C/switch proportional wins all four ours cells at lag 0 and 10 (-0.011 to -0.033 C), and the narrow on/off gate chatters 14-24 midpoint crossings per 180 min in 20 C rooms vs 1 for proportional. No control-theory prior work (P-only steady-state offset, bang-bang optimality with free actuation; Astrom and Murray) is cited, so the 'softness costs comfort' result is presented without noting it is the textbook expectation.

2 of 4 seeded mutants survive: removing the 0.1/0.2 C widths from grid() (the bands the headline says win) and making tau_range return (min, min) (which backs the 'full 0.15-0.80 range' claim). No test pins a tuned band or a results.txt number.
Win count uses x < 0, so the ref lag 5 'between' cell printed -0.000 is counted in '5 of 16'; at the printed precision it is a tie (4 strict wins).

'the same first-order lag' is a forward-Euler update tau += (cmd-tau)/lag on a 1-min step (inherited from garment-twonodeswitch); it responds faster than a continuous first-order lag (0.730 vs 0.712 after 10 min at lag 5; much more at lag 2) and is not stated.
run.py re-tunes the proportional band up to three times per lag/choice set (lines 18, 26, 32) instead of reusing the result; harmless but triples runtime of the tuning.

verdict: Reproducible and arithmetically right: run.py and figure.py regenerate results.txt and the SVG byte-for-byte, an independent implementation of both gates and the tuning loop reproduces the headline cells exactly, three closed-form checks match, and a finer grid confirms the negative result (proportional within 0.008 C of on/off). Every README number is backed. It does not meet the bar: verification is 2 (2 of 4 seeded mutants survive, including deleting the very bands the headline says win), and as research it is a one-module step that restates the textbook expectation (free actuation favours near-bang-bang; a wide P band adds offset) without citing control literature, while leaving open a question the upstream penalty sweep answers in seconds (at 0.01 C/switch proportional wins all four ours cells). Limitations are honest.
